subject: gunblade
pitch:
Category: Weapon.
Subject: gunblade.
Style: Final Fantasy.
reasoning:
I'm thinking about designing a gunblade prop, Final Fantasy style, as a static model that stands upright with its blade tip touching the floor at y=0.

I'm sketching out the blade geometry with a single-edged profile, a thin spine on one side, and a tapering width down to a sharp tip, defining the outline coordinates that will later get extruded into a 3D shape.

For the blade parts, I'm planning two layered extrusions: a main steel body with beveled edges where the cutting side gets a lighter, brighter paint and the fuller groove stays dark, plus a separate thicker spine bar running along the back. Then I'm moving into the gun-themed hilt section, starting with the guard block and the grip wrap above it.

I'm placing a revolver-style cylinder at the blade's base near the grip, complete with small dark chamber holes around its ring, along with a trigger guard torus, trigger, and hammer at the back of the hilt, plus a barrel rod running partway down the spine toward the muzzle. I'm keeping the hilt oriented vertically along the center axis.

I'm laying out the full gunblade's proportions bottom to top: tip at 0, blade extending to 0.80, a chamber block from 0.80-0.95, grip from 0.95-1.17, and pommel finishing at 1.25, matching Squall's oversized scale. The crossguard is a gold box with small wing-shaped extrusions on the edges, and I'm adding a decorative chain with a lion pendant dangling from the pommel, its links formed from small torus shapes.

I'm planning the surface textures next: a rune-like engraving on the blade face, a lion emblem decal, a crest on the cylinder chamber, and a grip-wrap pattern, plus a glowing blue gem embedded in the guard. I'm defining a reusable part-placement helper and confirming that static models don't need joints since there's no articulation required here.

Writing steel paint shader...

Setting blade thickness to 0.014 with engraving plane positioned just above the face. For the chamber piece, I'm sizing a cylinder slightly wider than the blade, positioned near the guard area with its axis along Z.

Still working out the cylinder geometry...

Now I'm positioning the trigger guard as a torus looping from the chamber down to the grip, with a small tilted box inside as the trigger itself, working out the exact coordinates so it clears the chamber geometry.

For the crossguard, since Squall's gunblade barely has one, I'm sketching a flared shield-shaped gold plate near the blade base with symmetric outline points, adding a glowing blue gem embedded at its center, and considering whether to add a decorative gold lion emblem on the guard or pommel disc.

Settling on placing the lion emblem as a small circular decal on the guard plate's front face, and moving the gems to flank positions on either side instead. For the chain, I'm plotting a catmull-rom path hanging from an attachment point near the pommel down through several link positions, though I notice it may overlap with the trigger torus geometry near the base.

Adjusting the chain path to offset slightly forward in z so it clears the body, ending in a small gold pendant disc with the lion motif, then generating the individual torus links along that curve with alternating orientation for a realistic chain-link look.

Now I'm detailing the grip wrap with steel bands and gold ring accents, deciding to skip the leather tail strap and blade-edge highlight for simplicity. I'm also planning a stylized gold lion head emblem and a vertical engraved rune-like text pattern for added decoration.

I'm adding a glowing blue gem accent and a matching pommel gem, plus dark chamber holes with small brass bullet caps poking out slightly. I'm nudging the whole model downward slightly so the blade tip sits properly at the lowest point without floating.

Still defining the blade outline...

Writing the paint shader...

I'm checking the available imports from the builder library—part creation, glow kit, and curve utilities. Then I'm setting up the cylinder geometry oriented along the z-axis and a flat torus for the guard, before sketching the hammer outline as a small curved extrusion shape.

Now I'm placing the ferrule, grip, and pommel sections along the handle's length, adjusting positions so each piece overlaps correctly—gold rings, a lathe-turned pommel profile, and a small gem fitted on top. I'm also planning to add engraving and decorative textures like a lion motif.

For materials, I'm defining gradient-based paint functions: a gold shader mixing warm tones with noise, a dark steel shader following similar logic, and a leather grip paint using diagonal wrap lines based on angle and position. With that settled, I'm ready to write the full module and export the metadata.
